title: warrant lane verdict
description: What one lane returns about one item. Consumed through Structured Outputs rather than a prefill, which current models reject. Three terminal states: pass, fail and inconclusive — and inconclusive is a valid terminal answer that routes to a person, not a retry, because measurement uncertainty has to be declarable. Note what is absent: the verdict carries no model id or version. The operator's pin in lanes.toml is authoritative for those, so a lane cannot report a model it was not run as, and additionalProperties is false so it cannot smuggle one in.

lane.description: The lane id from lanes.toml. lane_run.py rejects a verdict written for a different lane than the one it ran.

defect_class.description: A class named in the warrant. A class the warrant does not name defaults to tier 0, and no machine may close it.

evidence_digest.description: The digest snapshot_evidence.py printed before any judging. A verdict whose digest does not match the snapshot on disk is void.

kind.description: What sort of proposition this is. adjudicate.py routes a disagreement by kind: numeric to tick_and_tie.py, missing-element to lineage_gate.py, classification to taxonomy_check.py, anything else to a named person.

evidence.description: Where in the snapshot this is visible. A finding with no locatable evidence cannot be settled by a deterministic check.

uncertainty.description: Declared, not inferred. An inconclusive verdict must say why and what would settle it.

oneOf.description: Inconclusive, which is terminal too — and has to carry the reason and what would settle it, or it is a shrug rather than a result.
